Adam — thanks for the traceroute and heads-up. Short answers up-front: 1) we provide a small set of static egress IPs for the control-plane interactions and one optional NAT-bounced range for telemetry; 2) the private control plane does not require customer-side proxying, but customers often route through their egress proxy to capture telemetry; 3) SNI/TLS is preserved for all upstream calls and we recommend allowing TLS 443 with SNI passthrough.

I'll loop in Marissa and Jonas for the exact IP list and a short spreadsheet with port/flow expectations. We also have a runbook that describes how to configure network-level packet inspection without breaking our mutual TLS connection.

Action items for NovaCorp:
- Confirm whether you'll accept our static IPs directly or place Redwood behind your NAT (we can support both)
- If you use an egress proxy doing TLS interception, share the proxy cert chain and we will provide guidance on cert pinning for control-plane sessions

I'll send the IP list in a follow-up within the hour.

Subject: Re: Outbound controls for private endpoint deployment — final guidance and next steps

Thanks — good questions. Answers and next steps consolidated for your security and platform teams: 

1) TLS interception: Our control-plane and artifact fetch operations use standard TLS with SNI. We do not rely on client-side certificate pinning that would fail under typical enterprise TLS interception; however, for mutual TLS sessions (if you opt into customer-managed mTLS for extra security on artifact fetch), interception will break mTLS and is not supported. Recommended approach: allow SNI-preserving passthrough for control-plane (TCP 443) and place artifact fetches behind your NAT-bounced IP if you still need interception.

2) Authentication for artifact fetches: default is HTTPS with short-lived bearer tokens issued by the control plane. Optionally we support tenant-scoped mTLS for customers wanting certificate-based authentication. If you want mTLS, we'll exchange CSR/PKI details offline.

3) Binding a /28 NAT egress block: process and SLA
  - Send the egress IP CIDR in this thread (we will verify ownership and routability).
  - Redwood will perform a routing validation and bind the static egress mapping within 24 business hours for POC tenants; for production tenants we offer a formal change window with a 4-hour SLA on binding during business hours.
  - We will provide a short attest token (one-time) that you should display in your outbound SNAT manifest; this allows auditing and attribution of traffic to your tenant.

Action items (owners):
- Adam (NovaCorp): confirm whether you'll accept static Redwood IPs or provide a /28 NAT block. If NAT block, paste it here.
- InfraOps (NovaCorp): if you plan to intercept TLS, share the re-issuer CA chain and confirm which hostnames you will rewrite.
- Jonas (Redwood): create a binding request once Adam confirms and start the verification workflow (jonas_weber@redwood.example.com).
- David (Redwood): prepare a short runbook snippet showing how inspection teams can allow SNI passthrough for control-plane without losing telemetry.

We've attached the spreadsheet and linked the internal runbook for your security team. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the network team through the steps.
